concept.body: A sector (pie slice between two radii) claims the fraction θ/360 of the circle's whole area πr²: sector = (θ/360)πr². In radians the same formula reads ½r²θ = ½ · radius · arc. Note the contrast with arc length: area is quadratic in r, length is linear.

commonErrors.feedback: 28.27 ≈ 9π is the whole circle — 120° buys a third: ≈ 9.42.
6.28 ≈ 2π is the 120° ARC length — the area is (1/3)(9π) ≈ 9.42.

steps.body: The same fraction that priced the arc prices the **sector** — the pie slice between two radii. A θ-degree sector claims θ/360 of the circle's area πr² (Grade 7 again): **sector area = (θ/360) · πr²**. One fraction, two purchases: rim distance and interior area.

widget.prompt: Radius 6, central angle 90°. Sector area (2 decimals) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 113.1 ≈ 36π is the WHOLE circle's area — the sector claims a quarter: 9π ≈ 28.27.
9.42 ≈ 3π is an ARC LENGTH answer — area uses πr²: (1/4)(36π) ≈ 28.27.
14.14 ≈ 4.5π halves the slice — 90/360 is a quarter of 36π: ≈ 28.27.

widget.prompt: Radius 10, central angle 72°. Sector area (2 decimals) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 314.16 ≈ 100π is the full circle — 72° buys one fifth: 20π ≈ 62.83.
12.57 ≈ 4π is the 72° ARC LENGTH — the area formula squares the radius: 20π ≈ 62.83.

steps.body: Radian bookkeeping compresses this one too: with θ in radians, sector area = **½r²θ**. Check it on the quarter-circle: ½(36)(π/2) = 9π — the same 28.27. And notice the pleasing echo: arc s = rθ, sector = ½r·(rθ) = ½ · radius · arc, just like a triangle's ½ · base · height.

widget.prompt: Radius 4, angle 60° (= π/3 rad). Sector area by either formula (2 decimals) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 4.19 ≈ 4π/3 is the ARC length s = 4(π/3) — the sector is ½ · r · s = 8π/3 ≈ 8.38.
16.76 doubles — the ½ in ½r²θ is not optional: 8π/3 ≈ 8.38.
50.27 ≈ 16π is the whole circle — the 60° share is a sixth: ≈ 8.38.

steps.body: A sector is that same fraction of the area.

predict.prompt: A 90° sector takes a quarter of the circle's ARC. Does it also take a quarter of the AREA?

options.label: Yes — the same fraction of both
No — area scales by the square, so it takes a sixteenth
No — area is a smaller share, since the sector narrows toward the centre

predict.reveal: The same fraction of both. The k² rule governs SIMILAR figures scaled up; a sector is a SLICE of one fixed circle, so its angle takes the same share of everything — (1/4)(36π) = 9π. Open the angle and watch arc and area move in step.

widget.prompt: Radius 6. Open the angle to 90° and read the sector area.
widget.successFeedback: 90° is a quarter of the turn, so the sector is a quarter of the area: (1/4)(36π) = 9π ≈ 28.27 — and the arc is a quarter of the circumference, 3π. The SAME fraction governs both. One idea, two formulas, and neither needs remembering.
widget.lowFeedback: Not far enough — the sector is still under a quarter of the circle.
widget.highFeedback: Too far — you have opened past 90°.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate circle measurements while tangent, chord, radius, and power relationships update together.

widget.prompt: A sprinkler sprays water 8 m and sweeps through 135°. What lawn area does it water (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 201.06 ≈ 64π is the full circle — the sweep claims 135/360 = 3/8: 24π ≈ 75.4 m².
18.85 ≈ 6π is the ARC the spray's edge traces — the watered AREA is (3/8)(64π) ≈ 75.4 m².

widget.prompt: A sector of a radius-6 circle has area 15π. Find its central angle.

commonErrors.feedback: 47.12 ≈ 15π evaluates the AREA — the angle is its 360-share: (15/36)(360) = 150°.
75 halves — 15π out of 36π is 5/12, and 5/12 of 360 is 150°.
300 doubles — the circle's area is 36π (radius squared!), giving 150°.

takeaways: Sector area = (θ/360) · πr² — the degree share of the whole pie.
Radian form ½r²θ agrees, and reads as ½ · radius · arc.
Linear in θ but QUADRATIC in r — radius doublings quadruple slices.
steps.teaser: Finale: quadrilaterals whose four corners all touch the circle.
